newsitem.title: USA: Colorado winter wheat harvest nearly complete.
newsitem.headline: Colorado winter wheat harvest nearly complete.

text.p: The following is the weekly crop report from the Colorado Agricultural Statistics Service for the week ended Sunday, August 3.

SUMMARY for week ending August 3, 1997: Precipitation was widespread in Colorado and extreme amounts of rain was experienced in the northeast section. Flooding and crop damage was reported to fields and row crops in these areas. Due to the state wide moisture, farmers only averaged 3.6 days suitable for fieldwork for the week ending August 3, 1997.

Topsoil moisture supplies across the state are rated at 12 percent surplus, 57 percent adequate, 23 percent short, and 8 percent very short. Subsoil moisture supplies are rated at 17 percent surplus, 60 percent adequate, 18 percent short, and 5 percent very short.

Winter wheat harvest is nearly complete compared with last year's 95 percent and the average of 93 percent. Spring barley continues to mature and 28 percent of the crop has been harvested. The condition of the barley was reported as 17 percent excellent, 60 percent good, 18 percent fair, 4 percent poor, and 1 percent very poor. Harvesting of oats is 62 percent complete in comparison with last year's 52 percent and the five year average of 34 percent. Spring wheat turning color is at 75 percent, below the 1996 number of 99 percent but above the five year average of 63 percent. Harvest of spring wheat is 11 percent complete compared with last year's 17 percent and the five year average of 13 percent. The condition of the spring wheat was rated at 14 percent excellent, 66 percent good, 14 percent fair, 5 percent poor, and 1 percent very poor.
Summer potato harvest is just beginning and is 6 percent complete. This compares with last year's 10 percent and the five year average of 6 percent.

The condition of summer potatoes was rated at 17 percent excellent, 47 percent good, 24 percent fair, 7 percent poor, and 5 percent very poor. The fall potato condition was rated at 40 percent excellent, 40 percent good, 10 percent fair, and 10 percent poor. Dry beans flowered is at 80 percent, below the 1996 number of 85 percent but above the five year average of 58 percent. Seventy-three percent of the crop is in good to excellent condition. Sugar beet crop condition was rated at 19 percent excellent, 55 percent good, 17 percent fair, 6 percent poor, and 3 percent very poor. The onion crop condition was rated at 24 percent excellent, 59 percent good, 12 percent fair, 3 percent poor, and 2 percent very poor.

Corn silking is at 66 percent complete, compared to the 1996 number of 76 percent and the five year average of 53 percent. Twelve percent of the crop has reached the dough stage. The condition of the corn crop was rated at 19 percent excellent, 52 percent good, 19 percent fair, 7 percent poor, and 3 percent very poor. Sorghum is starting to head with 18 percent reported at this stage of development, compared to 17 percent headed at this time last year. Sorghum condition was rated at 9 percent excellent, 64 percent good, 18 percent fair, 5 percent poor, and 4 percent very poor. The second cutting of alfalfa is 77 percent complete. This compares to last year's 77 percent progress and the average of 58 percent. Pasture and range feed condition improved with the precipitation received during the week and the overall rating was mostly fair to good.
Colorado Crop Development/Condition Ratings for Week Ending 8/3
